af492574ef.q: Why does line manager training improve employee wellbeing in the workplace according to evidence?
af492574ef.a: There is evidence that training of line managers is one of the best things an organization can do to improve wellbeing in the workplace. Proper training enables managers to get the best out of people by setting high standards while also motivating and encouraging people to give their best, rather than simply complaining, criticizing, and challenging struggling employees. Getting the fundamentals right and providing managers with tools to enable their teams to flourish is at the root of good employment practices, improves productivity, and benefits everyone.

a21ecfda2a.q: What is Higher Health and how does it address prevention of mental health issues in young people?
a21ecfda2a.a: Higher Health is a third sector organization currently being trialled in Greater Manchester with the endorsement of Andy Burnham (now Prime Minister). The program gives young people soft skills essential for the workplace and securing employment, including reliability, empathy, interviewing skills, and how to offer the best of yourself at work, alongside understanding mental health and wellbeing. It combines digital programs with person-to-person learning and targets young people particularly in the NEET (not in education, employment or training) category who may not naturally gain these softer skills through family or school.

51b75aa79c.q: How does medicalizing normal human responses to difficult work environments fail to address root causes of workplace mental distress?
51b75aa79c.a: When someone is struggling in a toxic office environment—not sleeping and becoming stressed about work—they may visit their GP, who then prescribes antidepressants and potentially takes them out of work for weeks. However, this approach assumes the problem is in the person's brain rather than recognizing that the root cause is outside the person in the office environment. It merely dampens the senses without confronting the actual workplace problem, and people often end up remaining on antidepressants for long periods with potentially worrying side effects, while no one has actually fixed the toxic environment.

dd8f0b295d.q: What fiscal incentive did Norman Lamb propose to encourage employers to prioritize employee wellbeing?
dd8f0b295d.a: When he chaired a mental health commission in the West Midlands in 2018, Norman Lamb's commission proposed a 'wellbeing premium' where governments could give employers businesses a discount on their national insurance if they demonstrated they were focusing on employee wellbeing in the workplace. The idea is to incentivize rather than assume good behavior will happen naturally, encouraging employers to recognize that treating people properly, training line managers effectively, and behaving well results in more successful companies, improved productivity, and happier staff.

add2abda5b.q: What does the Keep Britain Working Review identify as the main workplace health challenge in the UK?
add2abda5b.a: Ill health and disability are becoming a bigger part of society due to an aging population and younger people developing mental health issues much earlier. This is leading to a large number of working age people becoming economically inactive. The current system fails because employers and workplaces are not very good at handling ill health and disability, causing people to leave work early instead of finding ways to stay in work.
add2abda5b.e: More employees than ever are off sick. What should employers do? With Sir Charlie Mayfield
add2abda5b.rq: We're trying to re-humanize the workplace. We've become very procedural and risk aware, but that can mean lack of contact and relationship between people, which if well supported could help thousands remain in work.

fd25485bde.q: What are the return-to-work statistics for employees absent from work due to health reasons according to the Keep Britain Working Review?
fd25485bde.a: If someone is away from work for 46 weeks, 96% return to work. Once absence reaches a year, less than 50% return. For people who become economically inactive for health reasons, there is only about a 3.8% chance of returning to work within the next year.

12493033ea.q: What is the potential economic benefit of improving workforce participation for people with health conditions or disabilities in the UK?
12493033ea.a: If the UK achieved the same level of participation as some G20 competitors, there would be approximately one million more people working. Even improving the participation rate by one percentage point would add 300,000 people to the workforce, equivalent to the size of Cardiff. This represents an opportunity running into billions of pounds annually in overall economic benefit.

a0da9d613d.q: What is the proposed workplace health system model and what are its key components?
a0da9d613d.a: The workplace health system is founded on shared responsibility between employers, employees, and government. Key components include: employers being actively engaged and on the pitch; developing return-to-work and stay-in-work plans; providing case managers to support difficult conversations; and enabling rapid access to early-stage treatment such as physiotherapy within a week or talking therapies for mental health issues.
